question:
(a) A north pole of a bar magnet is withdrawn from a closed coil. Explain the nature of the induced effect in the coil.
(b) Why must an external agent do work while withdrawing the magnet? Give reason.

options.A:
The induced current reinforces the decrease in magnetic flux and repels the withdrawing north pole.
No external work is required because the coil supplies energy to the magnet.
options.B:
The induced current produces a magnetic effect that opposes the decrease in flux, so the coil attracts the withdrawing north pole.
An external agent must do work against this attraction; this work is converted into electrical energy and heat in the coil.
options.C:
The induced current is absent because the magnet is moving away from the coil.
The external agent does work only against air resistance.
options.D:
The coil repels the withdrawing north pole to increase the decrease in flux.
The external work is stored permanently as magnetic energy.
